en.question: A classifier prompt works perfectly on ten hand-picked examples but scores 71% on a held-out set of 400. What is the most likely explanation?

options.text: The model version changed between the two measurement runs.
options.note: Possible, but a version change would usually move both numbers together.

options.text: The held-out set of 400 examples is substantially mislabelled.
options.note: Worth spot-checking, though a 29-point gap points at methodology first.

options.text: The prompt was iterated against those ten cases, so it overfits them.
Sampling temperature was set too low for a classification workload.
options.note: Temperature does not explain a systematic generalisation gap.

en.explanation: Tuning a prompt against the same cases you measure on is overfitting. Those ten stopped being an evaluation the moment they became the optimisation target; a held-out set must never be used for tuning.
